original_question: Let ν_1 and ν_2 be vector measures of finite variation with the same range R(ν_1) = R(ν_2), and assume that both variation measures |ν_1| and |ν_2| are perfect. Must ν_1 and ν_2 have the same Pettis differentiability behavior with respect to their own variations?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Problem 4.3 (Rodríguez-Piazza - Romero-Moreno): whether equality of ranges, together with perfectness of the variation measures, forces two vector measures of finite variation to have the same Pettis differentiability character with respect to their own variations.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly identifies the right open problem, keeps the hypotheses of finite variation and equal range R(ν_1)=R(ν_2), places the perfectness assumption on the variation measures |ν_1| and |ν_2|, and asks about Pettis differentiability relative to each measure's own variation.
missing_details: In the paper, a vector measure means a countably additive map ν:Σ→X defined on a σ-algebra and taking values in a Banach space.
The paper's standing convention is that Banach spaces are real.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it should say that ν_1 and ν_2 take values in the same Banach space X, so that R(ν_1) and R(ν_2) are equal as subsets of X.
The perfectness hypothesis applies to the scalar variation measures |ν_1| and |ν_2|, not to ν_1 and ν_2 themselves.
The phrase 'same Pettis differentiability character with respect to their variations' should be unpacked explicitly as an if-and-only-if statement.
If full self-containment is desired, Pettis differentiability should be spelled out as the existence of a Pettis integrable density f_i with ν_i(E)=∫_E f_i d|ν_i| for every measurable set E.
refined_question: Let X be a real Banach space, and for i=1,2 let ν_i:Σ_i→X be countably additive vector measures of finite variation on measurable spaces (Ω_i,Σ_i). Assume that R(ν_1)=R(ν_2) as subsets of X and that the scalar variation measures |ν_1| and |ν_2| are perfect in the usual measure-theoretic sense. Is the property of being Pettis differentiable with respect to its own variation measure determined by this common range; that is, must there exist a Pettis integrable f_1:Ω_1→X with ν_1(E)=∫_E f_1 d|ν_1| for every E∈Σ_1 if and only if there exists a Pettis integrable f_2:Ω_2→X with ν_2(E)=∫_E f_2 d|ν_2| for every E∈Σ_2?
justification: The exact target is Problem 4.3 in Section 4.1. The surrounding paragraph defines the relevant notation R(ν) and |ν| and explains the scope: the paper first recalls that equality of range determines finiteness of variation and, under that hypothesis, also determines Bochner differentiability with respect to variation; it then states that this fails in general for the Pettis integral and asks whether adding perfectness of the variation measures restores range-determined Pettis differentiability. Your draft is therefore already paper-faithful, and the only real refinements needed are to make the ambient real-Banach-space setting explicit and to unpack 'same Pettis differentiability character' into the precise yes/no property of admitting a Pettis density with respect to the measure's own variation.
